title: The Pet That Made a Millionaire

lines.text: This man got rich selling a pet
In nineteen seventy-five, Gary Dahl had an idea.
You see, a rock never needed feeding,
His customers could already find one outside.
So why would anybody pay for it?
Because Gary sold the whole joke.
Each rock came in a little carrier
with air holes and a bed of wood shavings.
He even included a training manual.
The price was three dollars and ninety-five cents.
And by Christmas, more than a million had sold.
Our skeptical shopper suddenly wanted two.
The craze faded the following year,
but Gary had become a millionaire.
Its owner was the one who fetched the money.

sources.supports: Gary Dahl, 1975; a stone sold in a carrier with wood shavings and a humorous training manual; over one million sold by Christmas; the fad ended in 1976.
Carrier air holes; retail price $3.95; the fad made Dahl a millionaire.

production_notes: Original comic dramatization. The shopper and reactions are fictional; no dialogue is presented as a historical quotation. The pet rock is drawn without a face to emphasize the joke. Target 40-60 seconds, 1080x1920, 30 fps.
